_about: Outcome of the independent translations in this folder: each was translated from the English only, without the live draft, and compared with the live text line by line. Lines where the meaning differed were checked to see which version was wrong.

ta.outcome: No meaning errors found in the live Tamil. Every meaning difference was an error in the independent version, e.g. 'scam' as 'sound' (quiz[1].title), 'account is locked' as 'is zero', 'cousin' as 'elder brother', 'scam mule' as 'source', 'MOM addresses' as 'MOM emails', 'gov.sg' senders said to 'start with' gov.sg, the work permit fine dropped from quiz[0], Korean characters inside Tamil words.

noted.feedback.csatQuestion: Live asks 'How was today's event for you?' where the English asks 'How happy...'; kept: it reads naturally with the happy/unhappy answer scale and came from an earlier SEA-LION suggestion.

my.outcome: No meaning errors found in the live Burmese. The independent version was much worse: 'scams' and 'scammers' as 'words' (event.title, event.intro), 'quiz' as 'representative', 'transfer money' as 'feed fish', 'caned' as 'managed', 'employer' as 'worker', 'cousin' as 'uncle', the feedback scale as 'love feeling', and Arabic, Thai, Georgian and Malay fragments inside Burmese words. The missing lines failed in every run (SEA-LION returned broken JSON for that batch); not pursued given the quality of the rest.

my-gemini.model: gemini-3.8-flash (free API tier; Pro was not available on the key)
my-gemini.outcome: Fluent, natural Burmese, far better than SEA-LION's; it agreed with the meaning of every live line. Two improvements applied: 'Dear worker' in the fake fine SMS used an affectionate 'dear' (ချစ်လှစွာသော, as to a loved one) and now uses the formal-notice opening လေးစားရပါသော; 'scam mule' stood alone in Latin script in 3 lines and now has the Burmese gloss ငွေလိမ်ကြားခံ, with 'scam mule' kept in brackets (glossary updated). Other differences are register only: Gemini's Burmese is more colloquial (မင်း, တယ်), the live text more formal written style (သည်, ပါနှင့်); kept.

ta-sarvam.outcome: No meaning errors found in the live Tamil. The independent version is colloquial with many English loanwords, and its meaning differences were its own errors, e.g. 'scam mule' as 'scam person', 'crime' as 'wrong', 'instead' as 'later', 'Licence' and 'sender' dropped, 'registration' for login, CHECK inserted into a scam message, a garbled penalties line.

noted.quiz[4].msg.bubbles[0][0].t: Live 'is going to cancel' vs English 'wants to cancel': slight shift, same threat; kept for length.
